items.descriptionHtml: <p>AWS Quick now supports assignments for custom permissions and limit profiles to groups from your enterprise identity provider (IdP).&nbsp;Administrators can now apply feature restrictions and per-user resource limits to IdP groups, in addition to the existing user, role, and account assignments. Quick enforces these limits automatically as users consume resources.<br> <br> When group-level assignments apply to a user who belongs to multiple groups, Quick resolves overlapping assignments as follows: for custom permissions, a capability denied by any group stays denied, and for limit profiles, the user receives the highest value for each limit type across those groups.<br> <br> Group assignments are available in Quick for Professional and Enterprise plans. For feature availability by AWS Region, see AWS <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quick/latest/userguide/regions.html#regions-qs" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Quick Regions</a>. items.descriptionHtml: <p>AWS Quick now includes enterprise guardrails, giving administrators configurable content safety and sensitive-information controls for user prompts. Administrators can apply guardrail policies to individual users or enterprise identity provider (IdP) groups or set a policy as the account default. User-level policies take precedence over group policies and account defaults. In this mode, Quick evaluates user prompts and logs policy matches without blocking requests, so administrators can assess the impact on business workflows and refine policies. When administrators enable enforcement, Quick blocks matching prompts and displays a message to the user. Administrators can review detected and blocked events in Amazon CloudWatch Logs.<br> <br> Enterprise guardrails are available in preview for select Quick customers with Professional and Enterprise plans. For feature availability by AWS Region, see <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quick/latest/userguide/regions.html#regions-qs" target="_blank">AWS Quick Regions</a>. To learn more, see the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quick/latest/userguide/guardrails.html" target="_blank">enterprise guardrails documentation</a>.</p>

items.descriptionHtml:
<p>Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) now supports Apache Kafka version 4.2 on Standard brokers. A key highlight of this release is Queues for Kafka, which is now production ready. With Queues, multiple consumers can process messages from the same topic partitions, which improves parallelism and throughput for workloads that need point-to-point message delivery. items.descriptionHtml: <p>Today, Amazon SageMaker AI announces cross-Region inference routing, which helps keep inference applications available when a region runs short of capacity by sending requests to endpoints deployed in other AWS Regions and AWS accounts. Models served on accelerated instances can reach capacity limits in a single Region, and an unhealthy endpoint can lead to throttling and errors for end users. Previously, teams had to build and maintain their own routing, health checks, and retry logic across Regions.<br> <br> With cross-Region inference routing in SageMaker AI, developers create an inference router, register the real-time endpoints, asynchronous endpoints, and inference components they already run, and point their applications at the router. The router prefers endpoints in its own Region, shifts new requests to healthy destinations in other Regions as errors rise, and returns traffic gradually after the local endpoint recovers. Existing endpoints, models, and containers do not change. Endpoint owners stay in control: an endpoint policy determines which routers in other accounts can use an endpoint, and an optional cross-Region traffic cap reserves capacity for the endpoint’s local callers. Each real-time response identifies the endpoint that served the request and the reason, and router metrics in Amazon CloudWatch show where traffic went.<br> <br> Cross-Region inference routing is available for real-time inference in 32 commercial AWS Regions, and for asynchronous inference in 25 Regions. There is no additional charge for cross-Region inference routing. Customers pay standard SageMaker AI pricing for the endpoints that serve requests and standard Amazon CloudWatch rates for router metrics. To learn more, see the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/inference-router.html">Amazon SageMaker AI Developer Guide</a> and <a href="https://aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/ai/deploy/">SageMaker AI Deployment page</a>.</p>

<p>Today, AWS announces the public preview of medical coding in <a href="https://aws.amazon.com/health/connect-health/">Amazon Connect Health</a>, a HIPAA-eligible AI service that works alongside healthcare teams across patient engagement and point-of-care workflows. items.descriptionHtml: <p>Today, AWS Quick is announcing the general availability of structured data connector restrictions through custom permissions. items.descriptionHtml: <p><a href="https://aws.amazon.com/ecs/">Amazon Elastic Container Service</a> (Amazon ECS) introduces json-file log driver support for Amazon ECS Managed Instances and log driver volumes for Amazon ECS Managed Daemons. Together, these features let you collect application logs with the observability agent of your choice and forward them to any destination you choose.<br> <br> With this launch, your application containers on ECS Managed Instances can write their logs as local files in standard Docker json-file format, which most observability agents read natively. Your managed daemons can directly read these files through a volume mount, without specifying host bind mount paths or requiring root privileges. As a result, one managed daemon on each instance can collect logs from every application container that uses the json-file log driver. Amazon ECS keeps each container's logs in a dedicated directory named with the container ID and retains them until the container is removed, so your managed daemon can use native file-based log collection and trace every log back to the container that produced it.<br> <br> To get started, set the log driver to json-file in the logConfiguration of your application task definition. Next, register a daemon task definition that specifies a volume with logDriverVolumeConfiguration, and mount the volume into your daemon container using mountPoints. You can configure this using the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, API, AWS SDKs or AWS CloudFormation. This feature is available in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon ECS Managed Instances and Managed Daemons are available, at no additional cost. To learn more, refer to our <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/managed-daemons-task-definitions.html#managed-daemons-volumes">documentation</a> page and visit <a href="https://aws.amazon.com/ecs/managed-instances/">Amazon ECS Managed Instances</a>.</p>

items.descriptionHtml: <p>AWS WAF announces automatic SDK integration for Amazon CloudFront distributions. Operations such as forward_backward(), optim_step(), and sample() become API calls against a live, stateful session, so customers compose whatever training procedure their technique requires while SageMaker AI handles GPU allocation, model and LoRA loading, distributed execution, fault recovery, checkpoint storage, and security.<br> <br> Customers can call these operations directly from their own Python code to drive reinforcement learning, supervised fine-tuning, or custom training objectives against a live session, with checkpointing and resume built in. Billing is per token processed, so local computation like reward scoring isn't billed as GPU time. SageMaker AI is also releasing the <a href="https://github.com/aws/sagemaker-training-sessions-cookbook">SageMaker training sessions cookbook</a>, a set of ready-to-run SFT and RL recipes customers can use as blueprints for their own training loops.<a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/customizing-models-training-sessions.html"></a></p> 
<p>Training session APIs are generally available today in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), and Asia Pacific (Mumbai). To get started, install the SageMaker Python SDK and clone the cookbook, or launch a notebook in SageMaker Studio and connect a coding agent. To learn more, visit the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/customizing-models-training-sessions.html">documentation&nbsp;</a>and the <a href="https://aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/ai/model-customization/">Amazon SageMaker AI webpage.</a></p>
